proofs.proof_tex:
Set
\[
 S_N(p,\gamma)=V_{0,N}(p)+V_{1,N}(p,\gamma),
 \qquad
 S(p,\gamma)=V_0(p)+V_\gamma(p).
\]
These quantities are nonnegative because they are Poisson energies.  The uniform energy convergence in Theorem \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\) gives
\[
 r_N:=\sup_{p\in\mathcal P,\,|\gamma|\leq G}
 |S_N(p,\gamma)-S(p,\gamma)|\longrightarrow0.                 \tag{16}
\]
For nonnegative \(x,y\),
\[
 |\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{y}|^2
 =\frac{|x-y|^2}{(\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{y})^2}
 \leq |x-y|,
\]
where the equality is interpreted by continuity when \(x=y=0\).  The staffing term \(c_M\gamma\) is the same in \(J_N\) and \(J\).  Definitions \(\mathrm{design\mbox{-}objective}\) and \(J_N\), (16), and the fixed positivity and finiteness of \(c_Iz_\alpha\) therefore imply
\[
 \Delta_N:=\sup_{p\in\mathcal P,\,|\gamma|\leq G}
 |J_N(p,\gamma)-J(p,\gamma)|
 \leq c_Iz_\alpha\sqrt{r_N}\longrightarrow0.                 \tag{17}
\]

Let \(\mu(p)=\inf_{|\gamma|\leq G}J(p,\gamma)\).  The oracle-conditional certificate theorem yields
\[
 J(p,\gamma_\epsilon)-\mu(p)
 \leq U_\epsilon-L_\epsilon
 \leq\epsilon.                                                \tag{18}
\]
Moreover, (17) implies
\[
 \inf_{|\gamma|\leq G}J_N(p,\gamma)
 \geq \inf_{|\gamma|\leq G}J(p,\gamma)-\Delta_N
 =\mu(p)-\Delta_N.                                            \tag{19}
\]
Applying (17) once more at \(\gamma_\epsilon\), and then using (18)--(19), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 J_N(p,\gamma_\epsilon)-\inf_{|\gamma|\leq G}J_N(p,\gamma)
 &\leq J(p,\gamma_\epsilon)+\Delta_N-\mu(p)+\Delta_N\\
 &\leq\epsilon+2\Delta_N.
\end{aligned}                                                  \tag{20}
\]
The convergence in (17) is uniform over \(p\in\mathcal P\), so \(2\Delta_N=o(1)\) uniformly.  This proves the stated oracle-relative finite-system regret bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
Conditional on a supplied input name and a supplied sound pair \((L_J,\mathfrak O)\) satisfying Definition \(\mathrm{interval\mbox{-}oracle}\) on every call made by Definition \(\mathrm{certificate\mbox{-}algorithm}\), for every rational \(\epsilon>0\) that algorithm terminates and returns a certificate \(\mathrm{Cert}\), an incumbent \(\gamma_\epsilon\in[-G,G]\), and rational numbers \(L_\epsilon,U_\epsilon\) such that
\[
 L_\epsilon\leq \inf_{|\gamma|\leq G}J(p,\gamma)
 \leq J(p,\gamma_\epsilon)\leq U_\epsilon,
 \qquad U_\epsilon-L_\epsilon\leq\epsilon.
\]
Every global minimizer, if one exists, lies in the certificate's unpruned interval cover, and every pruning decision is validated by a recorded oracle lower bound.  For \(G>0\), the full-level fallback makes at most \(2^{D_\epsilon+1}-1\) interval evaluations and fewer than \(3\cdot2^{D_\epsilon+1}\) interval-objective or point-oracle requests, all at precision at least \(m_\epsilon\).  For \(G=0\), one certified point evaluation suffices.  This theorem constructs no model-specific oracle and its certificate is checkable only relative to the supplied sound receipts.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 \mu=\inf_{|\gamma|\leq G}J(p,\gamma).
\]
The supplied oracle encloses the real-valued objective on every interval invoked by the algorithm, so \(\mu\) is finite.  We first suppose \(G>0\).  Every interval \(I\) in the complete bisection level of depth \(D_\epsilon\) has
\[
 \operatorname{diam}(I)=2G\,2^{-D_\epsilon}.
\]
By the definition of \(D_\epsilon\),
\[
 2^{-D_\epsilon}
 \leq \left(\max\{1,8GL_J/\epsilon\}\right)^{-1},
\]
and therefore
\[
 L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)
 =2GL_J2^{-D_\epsilon}
 \leq\frac{\epsilon}{4}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
The algorithm calls an oracle at depth \(r\) with precision at least \(m_\epsilon+r\).  Hence, at the terminal level,
\[
 e_\epsilon:=2^{-(m_\epsilon+D_\epsilon)}
 \leq2^{-m_\epsilon}
 \leq\frac{\epsilon}{8},                                      \tag{2}
\]
where the last inequality follows from the definition of \(m_\epsilon\).  The supplied oracle contract and (1)--(2) show that every terminal interval receipt has width at most
\[
 w_\epsilon:=L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)+e_\epsilon
 \leq\frac{3\epsilon}{8},                                    \tag{3}
\]
and that every terminal midpoint receipt has width at most \(e_\epsilon\).

Let \(U_t\) denote the incumbent upper endpoint at a finite stage and let \(U_\epsilon\) be the final incumbent.  An incumbent is an upper endpoint of a point receipt containing the corresponding objective value.  Consequently,
\[
 U_t\geq\mu,
 \qquad U_t\geq U_\epsilon.                                  \tag{4}
\]
If an interval \(I\) contains a global minimizer \(\gamma^*\), oracle inclusion gives
\[
 \underline J(I,m)\leq J(p,\gamma^*)=\mu\leq U_t.             \tag{5}
\]
The strict pruning rule \(\underline J(I,m)>U_t\) therefore never removes such an interval.  Thus every global minimizer, if one exists, remains in the final unpruned cover.  This argument uses neither convexity nor uniqueness nor an interior-minimizer condition.

We next prove that the terminal active family is nonempty and brackets \(\mu\).  If \(U_\epsilon>\mu\), then, for each \(\delta\in(0,U_\epsilon-\mu)\), the definition of the infimum supplies \(\eta_\delta\in[-G,G]\) with
\[
 J(p,\eta_\delta)<\mu+\delta<U_\epsilon\leq U_t.              \tag{6}
\]
Every ancestral interval containing \(\eta_\delta\) has lower receipt at most \(J(p,\eta_\delta)\), so (6) prevents its pruning.  Hence \(\eta_\delta\) belongs to an active terminal interval.  If \(U_\epsilon=\mu\), let \(u\) be the point furnishing the final incumbent.  Its point receipt contains \(J(p,u)\), whence
\[
 \mu\leq J(p,u)\leq U_\epsilon=\mu.                           \tag{7}
\]
Every ancestral interval containing \(u\) has lower endpoint at most \(J(p,u)\leq U_t\), so that interval is not pruned.  The active terminal family is therefore nonempty in either case.

Define \(L_\epsilon\) to be the minimum lower endpoint over active terminal interval receipts, as required by Definition \(\mathrm{capacity\mbox{-}certificate}\).  For any active terminal interval \(I\) and any \(\eta\in I\), oracle inclusion and (3) imply
\[
 \underline J(I,m)
 \geq J(p,\eta)-w_\epsilon
 \geq\mu-w_\epsilon.
\]
Taking the minimum over active intervals yields
\[
 L_\epsilon\geq\mu-w_\epsilon.                               \tag{8}
\]
If \(U_\epsilon>\mu\), the active interval furnished by (6) has lower endpoint at most \(J(p,\eta_\delta)<\mu+\delta\).  Since this holds for every sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), it gives \(L_\epsilon\leq\mu\).  If \(U_\epsilon=\mu\), the active interval from (7) has lower endpoint at most \(J(p,u)=\mu\).  Thus, in both cases,
\[
 L_\epsilon\leq\mu.                                         \tag{9}
\]

It remains to control the final incumbent.  The conclusion is immediate if \(U_\epsilon=\mu\).  Otherwise, choose \(\eta_\delta\) as in (6), let \(I_\delta\) be an active terminal interval containing it, and let \(u_\delta\) be the evaluated midpoint of that interval.  Since the same interval receipt contains both objective values, (3) gives
\[
 J(p,u_\delta)
 \leq J(p,\eta_\delta)+w_\epsilon
 <\mu+\delta+w_\epsilon.                                     \tag{10}
\]
The upper endpoint of the point receipt at \(u_\delta\) is at most \(J(p,u_\delta)+e_\epsilon\).  Since the final incumbent is no larger than any evaluated point upper endpoint, (10) implies
\[
 U_\epsilon<\mu+\delta+w_\epsilon+e_\epsilon.
\]
Letting \(\delta\downarrow0\) and applying (2)--(3), we obtain
\[
 U_\epsilon\leq\mu+w_\epsilon+e_\epsilon
 \leq\mu+\frac{\epsilon}{2}.                                 \tag{11}
\]
Equations (8), (9), and (11) now give
\[
 U_\epsilon-L_\epsilon
 \leq2w_\epsilon+e_\epsilon
 \leq\frac{7\epsilon}{8}<\epsilon.                            \tag{12}
\]
The selected \(\gamma_\epsilon\) is the incumbent point, so its point receipt and (9) yield
\[
 L_\epsilon\leq\mu
 \leq J(p,\gamma_\epsilon)\leq U_\epsilon.                   \tag{13}
\]

If an interval was pruned when the incumbent was \(U_t\), its recorded lower endpoint is strictly larger than \(U_t\), and (4) gives \(U_t\geq U_\epsilon\).  Therefore every pruned record satisfies \(\underline J_r>U_\epsilon\).  Equations (5), (9), (12), and (13), together with the retained oracle receipts, verify all semantic conditions in Definition \(\mathrm{capacity\mbox{-}certificate}\).

The complete binary tree through depth \(D_\epsilon\) contains
\[
 \sum_{r=0}^{D_\epsilon}2^r=2^{D_\epsilon+1}-1               \tag{14}
\]
nodes.  Thus the fallback makes at most this many interval evaluations.  There is at most one interval request and one midpoint point request per node, so the total number of requests is at most
\[
 2\bigl(2^{D_\epsilon+1}-1\bigr)
 <3\cdot2^{D_\epsilon+1}.                                    \tag{15}
\]
All precisions are at least \(m_\epsilon\), and pruning only reduces these counts.

Finally, if \(G=0\), the feasible set is \(\{0\}\).  Query the singleton at precision \(m_\epsilon\), set \(\gamma_\epsilon=0\), and take the rational receipt endpoints as \(L_\epsilon,U_\epsilon\).  The point contract and (2) give
\[
 L_\epsilon\leq J(p,0)\leq U_\epsilon,
 \qquad
 U_\epsilon-L_\epsilon\leq2^{-m_\epsilon}
 \leq\frac{\epsilon}{8}<\epsilon.
\]
This one-record certificate proves the assertion.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem proves the finite certificate semantics and worst-case termination count from the supplied oracle contract alone.
added_lemmas.gap: It deliberately does not construct the model-specific piecewise-Gaussian objective oracle.
added_lemmas.consumer: A sponsor may check the returned staffing certificate only after a sound oracle and its receipts have been supplied.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
From a supplied rational interval name \(\mathfrak r\) for \((p,c_M,c_I,\alpha,G)\), construct a positive rational \(L_J\) and, for every admissible rational interval \(I\subseteq[-G,G]\) and \(m\in\mathbb N\), rational endpoints \(\underline J(I,m)\) and \(\overline J(I,m)\), together with finite checkable evaluation witnesses derived from the piecewise-Gaussian Poisson-energy formulas for \(V_0\) and \(V_\gamma\), such that \((L_J,\mathfrak O)\) satisfies every enclosure, width, and point-width requirement of Definition \(\mathrm{interval\mbox{-}oracle}\) for \(J(p,\gamma)\).  In particular, the construction must certify the explicit uniform modulus
\[
 \overline J(I,m)-\underline J(I,m)
 \leq L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)+2^{-m}
\]
and must not take oracle soundness as an input premise.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current theorem conflates the unresolved construction of a sound piecewise-Gaussian objective oracle with the generic branch-and-bound implication.  The proposed claim isolates the logically narrower model-specific construction that the current claim already requires, while the conditional implication is proved separately.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Conditional on a supplied sound interval oracle and the certificate returned by Theorem \(\mathrm{oracle\mbox{-}conditional\mbox{-}capacity\mbox{-}certificate}\), uniformly for \(p\in\mathcal P\), the certified offset satisfies
\[
 J_N(p,\gamma_\epsilon)-\inf_{|\gamma|\leq G}J_N(p,\gamma)
 \leq\epsilon+o(1).
\]
The conclusion is oracle-relative: it supplies no unconditional model-specific staffing recommendation while construction of the sound piecewise-Gaussian objective oracle remains open.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The offset and its limiting-objective guarantee exist only relative to a supplied sound oracle and the generic certificate theorem while the model-specific Gaussian oracle construction remains open.

proposed.justification: This target records the unresolved model-specific step needed before the generic certificate can yield an operational staffing recommendation.
proposed.gap: A rational interval name and analytic Gaussian formulas do not by themselves provide sound rational enclosures, an explicit uniform modulus, or finite checkable evaluation witnesses.
proposed.consumer: Discharging this target would supply the sound oracle required by the conditional certificate and regret theorems.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct, from the supplied rational interval name and the piecewise-Gaussian Poisson-energy formulas, a sound rational objective oracle with an explicit compact-uniform modulus and finite checkable witnesses for every interval and point evaluation.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen core proves analytic diffusion and energy formulas but contains no validated rational enclosures for Gaussian normalization and tail terms, no interval treatment of the square-root energy composition and normal quantile, and no explicit rational derivative or Lipschitz bound from which the oracle-width contract follows.  Taking the oracle contract as a premise would assume precisely this crux.
open_obligations.attempted: Compact-uniform diffusion-energy convergence and analytic continuity were examined, but neither supplies low-level rational evaluation witnesses or an explicit certified modulus.  The logically separate branch-and-bound implication was completed under a supplied sound oracle.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The model-specific construction is not obtained from the frozen primitives.  The proved generic theorem shows that any supplied sound \((L_J,\mathfrak O)\) yields a terminating rational certificate with
\[
 L_\epsilon\leq\inf_{|\gamma|\leq G}J(p,\gamma)
 \leq J(p,\gamma_\epsilon)\leq U_\epsilon,
 \qquad U_\epsilon-L_\epsilon\leq\epsilon,
\]
and Theorem \(\mathrm{finite\mbox{-}design\mbox{-}regret}\) transfers that conditional guarantee to \(J_N\) with an additional \(o(1)\) term.  No unconditional machine-checkable staffing recommendation follows until rational enclosures, an explicit uniform modulus, and finite evaluation witnesses for the piecewise-Gaussian Poisson energies are constructed and verified.

prose_updates.tldr: For equal-arm stationary homogeneous marked-history service experiments, the paper derives a compact-uniform joint occupation-and-rate-score Gaussian law from exact finite-chain Poisson martingales.  Evaluating the exact stationary product law at the estimated rates while holding implemented capacity fixed yields fitted-center variance \(Q=A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A\), residual variance \(W=V-Q\), and uniformly valid Wald coverage for arbitrary joint divergence of \(N\) and \(T_N\).  The proved kink residual makes the diffusion center an \(O(N^{-1})\)-accurate corollary under \(T_N=o(N)\).  A generic branch-and-bound theorem gives finite certificate semantics conditional on supplied sound oracle receipts; constructing that oracle from the piecewise-Gaussian formulas with an explicit certified modulus remains open.

project_justification.gap: The operational-dosage anchor permits distinct fixed arm populations and capacity and gives separate fixed-system occupation and many-system fluid results.  It does not furnish the joint critical array law, marked-rate covariance, or exact fixed-capacity plug-in inference proved here for the narrower equal-arm stationary homogeneous subclass.  For capacity choice, neither the anchor nor the present frozen core supplies a validated rational oracle for the piecewise-Gaussian Poisson-energy objective.
project_justification.niche: The finite-source birth--death product law makes the implemented finite-system effect exactly computable at candidate rates, while critical capacity creates a piecewise-diffusion score correction and a nontrivial kink residual.  The design calculation separates generic, checkable branch-and-bound logic from the model-specific interval evaluation problem.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves stationary diffusion and Poisson-energy limits, a primitive martingale joint central limit law, the exact product-law fitted-center Wald theorem without a horizon upper bound, the uniform kink residual, and the diffusion corollary under \(T_N=o(N)\).  It also proves oracle-conditional rational branch-and-bound semantics and conditional finite-system regret, while isolating sound piecewise-Gaussian oracle construction as an unresolved model-specific obligation.

prose_updates.related_work: Boutilier, Jonasson, Li, and Yoeli allow distinct fixed arm populations and service capacity and establish separate fixed-system occupation and many-system fluid results.  This paper studies the narrower equal-arm stationary compact homogeneous marked-history critical subclass and derives a joint population-duration limit there; it does not claim that positive results transfer upward to the broader anchor class.  Braverman and Dai and Braverman inform the piecewise-diffusion and prelimit-Poisson residual methods.  Hafouta informs uniform triangular-array reasoning, although the exact martingale proof here needs no upper horizon exponent.  Wang and Plechac and Lok inform score--Poisson covariance and projection interpretations; the model-specific fixed-capacity derivative and exact product-law elbow are derived here.  Borst, Mandelbaum, and Reiman motivate square-root staffing.  Generic interval reasoning supports the conditional certificate theorem, but it does not supply the missing sound rational oracle, explicit Gaussian-energy modulus, or evaluation witnesses.  Li, Johari, Kuang, and Wager and Hays and Raghavan concern different congestion or interference models.
prose_updates.interpretation: The exact fitted interval targets the implemented stationary operational effect, not a diffusion estimand: at the true rates the product-law map equals \(\theta_N\) exactly.  Same-path rate fitting projects the empirical occupation fluctuation onto the marked rate scores, producing fitted-center variance \(Q\) and empirical-minus-fitted variance \(W=V-Q\).  The diffusion center is computationally simpler but inherits the additional \(T_N=o(N)\) condition from its proved \(O(N^{-1})\) approximation error.  If a sound objective oracle is supplied, the generic certificate and regret theorems validate its returned offset; absent that oracle, the paper makes no machine-checkable model-specific staffing recommendation.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The floating-point witness at \((\lambda,\tau,\nu,\gamma)=(1,1,1,0)\) remains diagnostic rather than a certified theorem output.  The kink residual is proved uniformly, including kink-crossing jumps and ceiling phases, and \(K_{\mathrm{res}}\) is a proved finite constant.  The unresolved computational step is to turn the supplied rational input name and piecewise-Gaussian Poisson-energy formulas into sound rational interval receipts with an explicit uniform modulus and finite checkable witnesses.  The branch-and-bound and regret results are conditional on those receipts.  Marked recovery causes, stationary initialization, independent equal-sized arms, homogeneous compactly positive rates, and a bounded critical staffing window remain substantive restrictions.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Exact finite-chain fitted centering and empirical inference require only \(N,T_N\to\infty\); no upper relation between duration and enrollment is imposed.  The diffusion fitted center differs by \(O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-1})\), so the proved route gives its Wald law under \(T_N/N\to0\).  The paper does not claim results for the anchor's unequal-arm class, unmarked histories, common shocks, arbitrary initialization, heterogeneous rates, vanishing-rate boundaries, post-assignment randomization inference, or clinical cure effects.  Capacity certification and finite-system regret are oracle-relative; construction of the required model-specific sound oracle remains open.
